note: Burnt Fen is a 6,940 ha drained fen with scattered Mesolithic findspots, not a single monument; only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family gives 52.46, 0.36, while GeoNames puts Burnt Fen about 6 km further east (52.45, 0.45) and the Suffolk HER gives only a grid square, so no second independent source can be quoted for the stored point.

Only the Wikipedia family (en/fr Tin Hinan Tomb articles, Wikidata Q3531165) prints a point for the tomb itself (22°53′08″N 4°52′05″E, a few metres from the stored point); GeoNames' matching point is typed as the hill, and Mapcarta prints no quotable coordinate pair, so no second independent source can be quoted.

The stored point is the town of Quillabamba and the Wikidata/Wikipedia point is exactly the village of Huyro (OpenStreetMap node at -13.00697, -72.55418), while Peru's tourism inventory (MINCETUR, via turismoperuano.com) places the Cochapata complex 17 km south-east of Huyro plus a 1.5 km walk; no source prints coordinates for the site itself, so two independent sources cannot be quoted.

The site is the Soyugbulaq kurgan cemetery, which the excavation report places '1km north of Soyugbulaq village' at a grid reference (8522404, 4578685, about 41.342, 45.266 in Pulkovo zone 8, roughly 2 km north of the stored point); the only quotable decimal/DMS coordinates (Wikipedia/Wikidata) are the village's, so no two independent sources give the cemetery's own point.

The stored point 48.6835, 30.3489 is the centre of the village of Sushkivka (Wikidata and the Ukrainian village pages give the same figure); the Trypillia settlement is only described as lying 'near the village' and no page that treats the settlement itself prints a point for it, the only decimal-degree pages being the village's or copies of the deleted Wikipedia article, so no two independent sources can be quoted for the site's point.

The ancient settlement lies at the southern edge of Ərəbyengicə village, about 200 m north of the Araz (Wikipedia; Azerbaijan National Encyclopedia), but the only published coordinates (enwiki 39°28′31″N 44°57′00″E, Wikidata 39.4737, 44.9657) are the village's, from one source family; no source gives the tell's own point.

Only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family prints a point for Ayawayq'u (13°19′13″S 72°05′36″W, 1.1 km from the stored point); Hostnig's rock-art survey on rupestreweb.info locates it only verbally (south face of cerro Capillayoq, Yucay District, 3100 m) and OSM has no node for it, so no second independent source gives the site's point.

Only the Megalithic Portal gives a point for the Rindu Hati statue group (3.961482S 103.410824E, GPS, 0.7 km from the stored point); the site has no Wikidata item or OpenStreetMap feature, and the former BPCB Jambi page is offline, so no second independent source can be quoted and the point is held for the owner.

Ngarrabullgan is an 18 x 6.5 km tabletop mountain whose rock shelters (Ngarrabullgan Cave, Nonda Rock) are not published with coordinates; Wikipedia gives the mountain as 16°52′S 144°45′E (the stored point) while GeoNames gives -16.8667, 144.7667, 1.8 km east, and no second independent source gives a point within 1 km of the stored one, so the point is held for the owner.

The site is the Inca wayrana/high-altitude shrine on the summit of Idmacoya (Inka Tampu) mountain north of Yupancca in Vilcabamba District; the MINCETUR records, the Wikipedia article and the UNSAAC thesis on Idmacoya give no coordinates, only Wikidata does, and it is not in OpenStreetMap, so no two independent sources for the point can be quoted.

The domus de janas lie by the Torre Argentina tower on the coast south of Bosa; nuraghi.net (from Nurnet NUR19616) prints 40.32089, 8.45074, 0.4 km from the stored point, and the Ministry's IDESE page pins them at 40.3215, 8.4448 only in its map script, not as page text; the Wikidata point (generic Domus de Janas item) is 50 km away and not this site. With only one quotable source the point is held for the owner; the stored point is consistent with both.

English Wikipedia gives 13.34694 S 72.24556 W, matching the stored point. Wikidata's -13.3922, -72.2028 is a coarse value 6.9 km away. OpenStreetMap maps the Wat'a archaeological site as an area centred about 400 m from the stored point, but no page prints that centre as a coordinate pair, and MINCETUR, the DDC Cusco and Newsweek give no coordinates. With only one quotable source family, the point is held for the owner.

The burials found in 2006 lie in the grave-and-settlement area Norum 202:1 (Holm 1:1/1:5, Norum parish), which RAÄ's register maps about 58.0675 N, 11.857 E, some 3 km south-east of the stored point (Wikipedia's point for the town of Stenungsund); no page prints that point as latitude/longitude, so no two quotable sources exist and the point is held for the owner.

Only the Wikimedia family (Wikidata and the Russian Wikipedia article, in Russian notation) prints a point for the theatre itself; OpenStreetMap-based Mapcarta gives 34.66419, 32.88789 but not in a quotable form, and the other pages give only the whole Kourion site, so no two independent quotable sources exist for the theatre's point.

The stored point (-14.145, -71.459) lies in Pampamarca District of Canas Province, Cusco, which shares only its name with the real location. Warahirka (Huarajirca) is in Pampamarca District of Yarowilca Province, Huánuco, about 550 km north. OpenStreetMap has the archaeological site 'Huarajirca' at -9.7263889, -76.6775 (source ign.gob.pe), but no second independent family (Wikipedia has no coordinates; MINCETUR, GeoNames and the Megalithic Portal give none) provides a point, so it is held for the owner with that lead.

The site is the Moylehid (Eagle's Knoll) passage-tomb cairn on Belmore Mountain, recorded only by Irish grid reference (H1499 4161, about 0.6 km from the stored point). The decimal points that can be quoted (Wikipedia, the Gazetteer of British Place Names) are the townland's, not the monument's, and the Megalithic Portal has no entry, so no two sources give the site's own point.

The site is the archaeological landscape of the Llanos de Moxos, earthworks spread over 110,000-200,000 km2 of the Beni Department; neither Wikipedia nor any scholarly page gives a single point for it, so no two sources can be quoted for the site's point and it is held for the owner.

The Wikidata item's point (34.0875, 36.117778) belongs to Qasr el Banat near Chlifa, a different site that the English article conflates with Qsarnaba. Vici.org places the Roman temple at Qsarnaba at 33.913345, 35.990585, 0.05 km from the stored point, and Aliquot and German Wikipedia put the temple in the centre of the village, but no second independent page prints coordinates for the temple itself, so the point is held for the owner.

The find site (the spear pedestal Schöningen 13 II-4 in the lignite mine) lies at about 52.1335, 10.9893 per German Wikipedia, Wikidata and OpenStreetMap, some 0.4 km from the stored point, but only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family prints it in a quotable form; OSM-based pages give no clean coordinate pair and the UNESCO tentative-list entry cannot be read by the checker, so no second independent source can be quoted.

Only the Wikipedia family prints a point for the Öküzlü ruins: English Wikipedia gives 36.56667°N 34.16111°E and German Wikipedia 36° 33′ 59″ N, 34° 9′ 39″ O, both about 0.1 km from the stored point. AroundUs repeats the Wikidata value, and the Mersin University survey page, Kültür Envanteri and the ministry pages print no coordinates, so there are not two independent sources.

The site is the Roman fort Derventio on the northern edge of Papcastle. Only Vici.org prints decimal coordinates for the fort (54.671215,-3.381792, about 0.15 km from the stored point); the Wikipedia and Wikidata coordinates are the village's, the Derventio article and its Wikidata item carry none, and other pages give grid references only, so no second independent source can be quoted.

The stored point is the summit of Intikancha mountain as Wikipedia and Wikidata give it; the only independent readable map feature, an OpenStreetMap peak, is also the mountain and carries the Wikidata link. The archaeological site, a small walled outpost called Ticona or Inticancha on a spur of Cerro Pucarani in Arkush and Ikehara's closed-access Nawpa Pacha paper, has no readable source giving its own point, so the point is held for the owner.

The stored point (47.6026, 28.5064) lies in Moldova, far from the site, which is the Trypillia mega-settlement Hlybochok (Glubochek) near Hlybochok village in Cherkasy Oblast (village about 48.867 N, 30.799 E; the settlement lies at the village's western edge and north of it, so its own point is roughly 2 km from the village centre). The only figure for the settlement itself that I found (Ohlrau and Rud 2019, 48 deg 53' 14.41'' N, 30 deg 47' 32.12'' E) is on ResearchGate, which a plain GET cannot read, and no second independent readable page prints the site's own point; village coordinates are not the site's point, so it is held for the owner.
